 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. This miscellaneous first appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act' for short) is filed by respondent No.2- Insurance Company challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 18.02.2019 passed in MVC No.1211/2015 on the file of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal No.13, Vijayapur, by which the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition filed under Section 163-A of the Act by the petitioners granting compensation in a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest at 9% p.a., and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS: Petitioners are the parents of deceased Noor Mohammad.

It is the case of the petitioners that on 29.11.2014, at about 1.00 p.m., deceased Noor Mohamad was traveling in TATA ACE vehicle bearing registration No.KA-28/B-1483 ('the offending vehicle' for short) along with goods for the purpose of centering work from Talikote to Malgaon village.
After passing B. Bagewadi and proceeding towards Muttagi village.
The driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner.
As a result of the same, he lost control over the vehicle and it toppled.
In the said accident, Noor Mohammad sustained grievous injuries and died on being admitted to Civil Hospital Vijaypur.
He was aged about 20 years and was doing centering work and earning Rs.40,000/- per annum.
Petitioners were dependant on him.
As the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and hence, the petition.

sentences.text: Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have appeared through counsel and have filed separate written statement disputing the age, occupation and income of the deceased and that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No.1 has pleaded that since the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.2, it is liable to pay compensation.
Respondent No.2 has further contended that offending vehicle is a goods vehicle.
At the time of accident, deceased Noor Mohammad and others were traveling in it as gratuitous passengers.
The driver of the vehicle is not holding a valid driving licence and as such, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition as against it.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. In support of their claim, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW-1 and one witness is examined as PW-2.

They have relied upon Exs.P-1 to 12.
8.
On behalf of respondent No.2, one witness is examined as RW-1 and Exs.R-1 and 2 are marked.

9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest at 9% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.
10. Petitioners have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

11. Respondent No.2 has challenged the impugned judgment and award contending that it is illegal,
incorrect, perverse, capricious, arbitrary and as such, liable to be set aside.
It is contrary to the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The impugned judgment has been passed mechanically and without application of mind.

The Tribunal has erred in overlooking the evidence on record, viz.,
evidence of RW-1 that at the time of accident, deceased and others were traveling in the goods vehicle as gratuitous passengers, which fact is evident from FIR, Complaint and Charge sheet.
11.1
No goods were being carried in the said vehicle and the same has been pleaded only to overcome the fact that it was in violation of the terms and conditions of the Policy.

The Tribunal has also ignored the fact that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle that at the time of accident, he was not possessing valid driving licence and plied the vehicle without fitness certificate.
Since there is violation of terms and conditions, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to allow the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and award.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for the petitioners supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.
13. In support of his arguments, he relied upon the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of M/s. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Smt. Salma and Others1.

sentences.text: The petitioners have filed petition under Section 163-A of the Act seeking compensation for the death of their son in the motor vehicle accident dated 29.11.2014 while traveling in a TATA ACE goods vehicle.
It is not in dispute that the offending vehicle is a goods vehicle.
It is also not in dispute that at the time of accident, along with deceased Noor Mohammad, 6 other persons were also traveling.
In the petition, petitioners have pleaded that at the time of accident, deceased was carrying goods for the purpose of building construction (centering) work.

However, 2008 (2) KCCR 675 (DB) it is not made clear what exactly was the material being carried in the offending vehicle,
which is admittedly a goods vehicle.
16. The accident took place at 1.00 p.m. and the complaint came to be filed at 8.00 p.m.
The complainant, Syed Suleman is one of the inmates of the offending vehicle.
In the complaint, at the end of paragraph No.2, a sentence is added that in the offending vehicle material used for centering work were being carried.

However, in the spot mahazar, which refers to the presence of the offending vehicle at the place of incident, there is no reference as to any goods being carried in the said vehicle or at least instruments used for centering work is carried.
17. In the charge sheet also, there is no reference to any goods being carried in the offending vehicle or that instruments i.e., tools used for construction work is being carried.

Of course as per Ex.P-12,
during the course of his statement before the Police, petitioner No.1 has chosen to give a statement that the articles used for centering work were being transported in the offending vehicle.

However,
in the light of the fact that no such goods or tools were found being carried in the offending vehicle,
in the charge sheet, there is no reference to it.
18. PW-2 - Mohammed Rafeeq is also an inmate of the offending vehicle.
He has deposed that in the offending vehicle, goods meant for purpose of building construction (centering) work were being transported.
He has deposed that after the accident, the said goods such as wood planks, bamboos and steel plates fell down.
Since PW-2 is the eye witness to the incident, his evidence is relevant.
During his cross examination, it is elicited that before he boarded the offending vehicle, six persons were already there.

If at all any construction material or any tools for centering work was being carried in the goods vehicle and deceased was traveling along with them, as the owner of the said goods, there would have been no occasion for remaining six persons to travel in the said vehicle.

The very fact that including the deceased, seven persons were traveling in the offending vehicle when the incident took place goes to show that it was being used for traveling and deceased and others were traveling in the same as gratuitous passengers.

Only for the purpose of overcoming the hurdle of getting the compensation from respondent No.2, as an after thought, it is pleaded that some construction material for the centering work were being transported in the said vehicle.

In fact a suggestion is made to RW-1 that after the accident, some unknown persons have removed the goods which were carried in the said vehicle, which supports the defence of respondent No.2 that deceased and others were traveling in the offending vehicle as gratuitous passengers and only to get compensation from respondent No.2, a false contention is being taken that centering material were being transported in the offending vehicle.
19.

The Tribunal despite examining all the evidence placed on record has wrongly held that deceased was not a gratuitous passenger and that there is no violation of the terms and conditions of the The Branch Manager vs Yaseen And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22550493/
4 policy.

sentences.text: Of course in the light of Ex.P-11 which is the driving licence of the driver of the offending vehicle, the contention of respondent No.2 that the offending vehicle was being driven by a person without valid licence is negated.
Of course, Ex.P-11 is a LMV-Non transport licence.

However, in the light of decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2, the driver of the offending vehicle is competent to drive the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. However, the material placed on record establish the fact that at the time of accident, deceased and others were traveling in the offending vehicle which is a goods vehicle as gratuitous passengers and as such, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.

In Salma's case referred to supra relied on by the petitioners, the question involved is whether petition under Section 163-A of the Act is maintainable even when the accident occurred due to the negligence of the victim.

In the present case, there is no (2017) 14 SCC 663 negligence on the part of the deceased and the issue involved in the present case is whether a gratuitous passenger is entitled for compensation at the hands of the insurance company while traveling in a goods vehicle.
Therefore, this decision is not applicable to the case on hand.

21. In the light of the evidence placed on record, the findings of the Tribunal is perverse and as such,
it is liable to be set aside so far as directing respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.

Of course, as the owner of the offending vehicle, it is respondent No.1 who is liable to pay the compensation and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) Appeal filed by respondent No.2/Insurance Company is allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment and award is set aside so far as directing respondent No.2 to pay the compensation is concerned.
iii) However, respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation with accrued interest, within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.

iv) Respondent No.2 is at liberty to withdraw the amount in deposit (if any).
v) The Registry is also directed to transmit the trial Court records along with copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
Sd/-
